messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 502/504 spike detected at api-gateway-edge.prod. Failure rate 502/504 = 8.6% over 5m, p50 latency increased. Paging @sre-oncall and @lena for triage. Link: https://observability.redwood/prod/alerts/1719807654

sre-oncall: On it. hopping into a bridge. Can someone grab a quick impact delta (customers/paths)?

lena: I see the surge on edge nodes in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Errors concentrated on route `/v1/generate` and `/v1/chat` behind the edge proxy. Starting with edge-proxy logs + upstream health.

matt: adding what I see from LB metrics: 5xx spike aligns with a burst of long-lived connections from a partner IP range. Connection count jumped ~3x at 1719807450.

incident-bot: Created incident channel #inc-1719807654, bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/1719807654, severity: SEV2. Notifying support.

support_lead: Support is seeing a handful of customers reporting timeouts and 502s. Triage question: is this internal or a downstream flapping?

lena: quick check: upstream model serving pods show normal CPU/GPU utilization, only a few 5xx in their logs. Primary suspect is the edge proxy (nginx/ingress) returning 502 on timed out upstream connections. Fetching edge logs now.

infra-bot: Recent deploy: `edge-proxy:v3.14.0` at 1719799000. No config changes since then. Autoscaling events: none.

lena: log snippet from edge-proxy (tail):
```
[1719807426] upstream timed out (110) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.5.87, server: api-gateway-edge, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://upstream-10.0.12.54:8080/", host: "api.redwood.ai"
[1719807451] 502 returned to client, request_time: 31.12s, upstream_response_time: 31.10s
```

lena: lots of `request_time` near ~30s, which matches the client's socket timeout in the proxy. Upstream seems to be responding but >30s.

sre-oncall: Are those requests normally that long? Check typical response times for these routes.

matt: baseline p95 for `/v1/generate` is ~1.6s. This is an outlier. The burst seems correlated with a small set of partner IPs as I said. Could be a bot or a bad client holding connections open.

lena: I recommend immediate mitigation: 1) increase `proxy_read_timeout` temporarily to 60s to avoid cutting in-progress long requests (risk: tying worker threads), OR 2) apply rate-limit / per-IP connection limit at edge for partner ranges, OR 3) divert traffic for the affected partner range to a lower-capacity pool with higher timeouts. Suggest doing (2) + (3) to preserve service for other customers.

ops_lead: Agreed. Start with rate-limiting offending IP ranges and enable a routing fallback to edge-fallback pool. I'll coordinate with infra.

ops_lead: Commands I'll run: `kubectl annotate svc edge-proxy --overwrite routing=limit-partner-range` then apply nginx acl for that CIDR. Also starting gradual traffic shift using our router: `redwood-router shift --from edge-seed --to edge-fallback --cidr 203.0.113.0/24 --rate 20% --duration 5m`

matt: tagging the suspicious CIDR 203.0.113.0/24 as source. Do we have a quick ACL entry?

lena: adding nginx config snippet to add `limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=addr:10m;` and `limit_conn addr 20;` for that location block will cap concurrent conns.

sre-oncall: Can infra apply the limit and start a targeted shift? If we see successful drop in 5xx we can keep changes and consider longer-term rate-limits.

infra-bot: Rate limit patch rolled to canary nodes (2/12) for the CIDR. Router shift command queued.

matt: after canary roll: 5xx rate dropped from 8.6% -> 2.1% in 3m. p95 latency improving.

support_lead: Notifying affected customers with a short blurb: "We're experiencing elevated 502/504 errors affecting a subset of requests. We're mitigating the issue and will provide updates every 15 minutes."

ops_lead: Rolling the ACL to all edge nodes now. Continuing traffic shift until the CIDR accounts for <0.5% of edge traffic or errors subside.

lena: Note: increasing timeouts would un-block those requests but would also tie up workers and degrade latency for others. The rate-limit+shift was lower-risk.

incident-bot: Update: mitigation in progress. 5xx rate trending down. Next update in 10m. Severity remains SEV2.

sre-oncall: Preparing a short RCA checklist: capture full upstream logs for the affected time window, enumerate customers for CIDR, correlate with recent partner changes, and check for retry storms. Also start retention of full request traces for 24h.

matt: I exported request traces for 1719807200-1719807800 and pushed to the incident bucket `s3://inc-1719807654/traces/`.

support_lead: Added impacted customer IDs to the incident doc and opened a prioritized support ticket list.

ops_lead: Handoff planning: I'm going to hand to night oncall in 15m once mitigation is stable. If the 5xx rate stays <1% for the next 10m, we'll move to monitoring and document steps.

sre-oncall: Acknowledged. I'll stay for the bridge till handoff. If anything regresses, page pager.

lena: quick note for postmortem: consider per-route adaptive timeouts and per-client flow control at the router to avoid single-client amplification causing edge resource exhaustion.

incident-bot: Timeline note added to incident doc. Current status: mitigated -> monitoring. bridge remains open for 30m.

ops_lead: :thumbsup: Good job everyone. Preparing a short customer summary for the status page and support queue.

sre-oncall: final check before handoff: 5xx = 0.9% over last 5m, p95 latency back to 2.0s. Moving to watch. Handoff to night-oncall `sre-oncall-2` at 1719807780.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded. If re-escalation needed, use `@incident-bot re-open 1719807654`.

support_lead: Will send update to affected customers now.

lena: leaving a TODO in the incident doc: schedule a follow-up to harden edge-proxy rate-limiting and alerting for per-CIDR surge.

ops_lead: End of active triage. Monitoring and post-incident tasks assigned. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
